questions.stem: The following is a list of data: $6; 11; 13; 2; 6; x$. Determine the value of $x$ if the mean of all six values is $7$.

canonical_solution.text_md: The mean is the sum of the values divided by how many values there are. This list has 6 values, counting $x$.
Add the values we know: $6+11+13+2+6=38$. The sum of all six values is therefore $x+38$.
Put this into the mean: $\begin{aligned}7&=\frac{x+38}{6}\\x+38&=7\times 6\\x+38&=42\end{aligned}$
Subtract $38$ from both sides: $\begin{aligned}x&=42-38\\x&=4\end{aligned}$
Check: $\frac{38+4}{6}=\frac{42}{6}=7$, so $x=4$ gives the mean $7$.

questions.stem: Sipho stands on the roof of a block of flats that is $80$ m high. From there he looks down at the base of a cellphone tower that stands on the same level ground as the block. The angle of depression of the base of the tower, from Sipho, is $40^\circ$. How far is the base of the tower from the base of the block of flats, to the nearest metre? (Treat Sipho as a point on the roof.)

canonical_solution.text_md: Draw a horizontal line from Sipho on the roof. The angle of depression, $40^\circ$, is measured from this horizontal line down to his line of sight to the base of the tower. It is not measured from the vertical.

The horizontal line is parallel to the ground, so the vertical drop from it to the base of the tower equals the height of the block, $80$ m. Let $d$ be the horizontal distance from the block to the tower. The right-angled triangle has the angle $40^\circ$ at Sipho, the side of $80$ m opposite it, and the side $d$ adjacent to it.
$\begin{aligned}\tan 40^{\circ}&=\frac{80}{d}\\d&=\frac{80}{\tan 40^{\circ}}\\&\approx 95.34\end{aligned}$
To the nearest metre, the base of the tower is $95$ m from the base of the block of flats.

$6 = \frac{1}{2}(3) \times SN$, so $SN = \frac{2 \times 6}{3} = 4$ cm. $S$ is the mid-point of $MN$, so $MN = 2 \times 4 = 8$ cm.
$MR = 2 \times ST = 2 \times 3 = 6$ cm.
Area of $\triangle MNR = \frac{1}{2} \times MR \times MN = \frac{1}{2}(6)(8) = 24$ cm$^{2}$.
Area of $MSTR$ = area of $\triangle MNR$ $-$ area of $\triangle SNT = 24 - 6 = 18$ cm$^{2}$.

$N\hat{S}T = \hat{M} = 90^{\circ}$ (corresp $\angle$s; $ST \parallel MR$), so $\triangle SNT$ has a right angle at $S$ and its area is $\frac{1}{2} \times ST \times SN$.
$8 = \frac{1}{2}(2) \times SN$, so $SN = \frac{2 \times 8}{2} = 8$ cm. $S$ is the mid-point of $MN$, so $MN = 2 \times 8 = 16$ cm.
$MR = 2 \times ST = 2 \times 2 = 4$ cm.
Area of $\triangle MNR = \frac{1}{2} \times MR \times MN = \frac{1}{2}(4)(16) = 32$ cm$^{2}$.
Area of $MSTR$ = area of $\triangle MNR$ $-$ area of $\triangle SNT = 32 - 8 = 24$ cm$^{2}$.

Multiply the area of the base by the height of the cylinder: $V = \text{area of base} \times \text{height} = 30.25\pi \times 18.5 = 559.625\pi \text{ cm}^{3}$

Write the final answer: the volume of the cylinder is $1758.11$ $\text{cm}^{3}$.

The base is a circle of radius $9$ cm, so its area is $\pi r^2 = \pi \times 9^2$.

The walls have area $\pi r h$, where $h$ is the slant height, the length along the wall from the apex to the edge of the base. Here that is $15$ cm, not the vertical height of $12$ cm: $\pi \times 9 \times 15$.

Adding the two areas gives $\pi \times 9^2 + \pi \times 9 \times 15$. Leaving out the base, using the vertical height in place of the slant height, or using the cylinder's wall area $2\pi r h$ would each give a different value.

questions.stem: A solid is made by placing a square-based pyramid on top of a cube. The edges of the cube are $12\text{ cm}$ long and the base of the pyramid is exactly the top face of the cube. Each triangular face of the pyramid has a slant height of $11\text{ cm}$ (the height of that triangle, measured from the middle of its base edge up to the apex). Calculate the total surface area of the solid, that is, the area of all the faces on the outside of the solid. Give your answer in $\text{cm}^{2}$.

canonical_solution.text_md: The top face of the cube is covered by the pyramid, and the base of the pyramid is covered by the cube, so neither is part of the outside of the solid. The exposed faces are the bottom face and the four side faces of the cube (five squares) and the four triangular faces of the pyramid.
Area of the five squares: $\begin{aligned}A_{\text{five squares}}&=5\times s^{2}\\&=5\times(12)^{2}\\&=720\text{ cm}^{2}\end{aligned}$

Area of the four triangles (each has base $12\text{ cm}$ and height equal to the slant height $11\text{ cm}$): $\begin{aligned}A_{\text{four triangles}}&=4\times\frac{1}{2}bh_{s}\\&=4\times\frac{1}{2}(12)(11)\\&=264\text{ cm}^{2}\end{aligned}$
Total surface area: $\begin{aligned}A_{\text{total}}&=A_{\text{five squares}}+A_{\text{four triangles}}\\&=720+264\\&=984\text{ cm}^{2}\end{aligned}$
Therefore the total surface area of the solid is $984\text{ cm}^{2}$.

questions.stem: A box contains coloured blocks: 31 purple, 26 orange, 30 white and 27 pink. A block is selected at random. Which of the following is the probability that the block is purple?

canonical_solution.text_md: First we work out how many blocks there are in total. This gives us the sample space: $n(S)=31+26+30+27=114$ .
The event is that the block is purple. There are $31$ purple blocks, so $n(E)=31$ .
Every block is equally likely to be selected, so: $\begin{aligned}P(\text{purple})&=\frac{n(E)}{n(S)}\\&=\frac{31}{114}\end{aligned}$ This fraction is already in simplest form.

The four colours are not equally likely, because there are different numbers of blocks of each colour, so the answer is not $\frac{1}{4}$ . The total $114$ counts all the blocks, not only the ones that are not purple, and the numerator counts the purple blocks, not the others.

A child from the class is selected at random. What is the probability that the child is a girl who is at least 4 years old? Write your answer as a fraction in its simplest form.

canonical_solution.text_md: The number of possible outcomes is the number of children in the class: $n(S)=6+10+6=22$ .
The rest of the children at each age are girls. The number of girls aged 4 is $10-4=6$ and the number of girls aged 5 is $6-2=4$ .
A girl who is at least 4 years old is a girl aged 4 or a girl aged 5, so $n(E)=6+4=10$ .
Finally, we can find the probability: $\begin{aligned}P(E)&=\frac{n(E)}{n(S)}\\&=\frac{10}{22}\end{aligned}$
Both $10$ and $22$ can be divided by $2$ , so in simplest form $P(E)=\frac{5}{11}$ .
Therefore, the probability that the child is a girl who is at least 4 years old is $\frac{5}{11}$ .

Count the positive trials: Team 1 won $ 2 $ matches and drew $ 4 $ matches, so $p=2+4=6$.
Calculate the relative frequency: $f=\frac{p}{t}=\frac{6}{10}=0.6$

Check by multiplying out: $(x - 9)(x + 10) = x^{2} + 10x - 9x - 90 = x^{2} + x - 90$, which is the expression we started with.

The bracket is a difference of two cubes, because $1 = (1)^{3}$ and $64z^{3} = (4z)^{3}$. The cube roots are $1$ and $4z$.
Write the whole factorisation, with the common factor in front: $6z - 384z^{4} = 6z(1 - 4z)(1 + 4z + 16z^{2})$

questions.stem: Factorise: $24x^{3} + 3y^{3}$

canonical_solution.text_md: The largest number that divides both $24$ and $3$ is $3$, so take out the common factor $3$ first: $24x^{3} + 3y^{3} = 3(8x^{3} + y^{3})$
Write each term in the bracket as a cube: $8x^{3} = (2x)^{3}$ and $y^{3} = (y)^{3}$. The bracket is a sum of two cubes with cube roots $2x$ and $y$.
Use $a^{3} + b^{3} = (a + b)(a^{2} - ab + b^{2})$ with the cube roots in place of $a$ and $b$: $8x^{3} + y^{3} = (2x + y)[(2x)^{2} - (2x)(y) + (y)^{2}]$
Simplify the second bracket and keep the common factor in front: $24x^{3} + 3y^{3} = 3(2x + y)(4x^{2} - 2xy + y^{2})$

Factorise the sum of cubes: $x^3 + 2^3 = (x + 2)(x^2 - 2x + 2^2) = (x + 2)(x^2 - 2x + 4)$.

Write all the factors together: $a(x^3 + 8) + b(x^3 + 8) = (a + b)(x + 2)(x^2 - 2x + 4)$.

Factorise every numerator and denominator: $x^2+9x+18=(x+6)(x+3)$, $x^2-9=(x-3)(x+3)$, $2x^2+12x=2x(x+6)$ and $32x^2-96x=32x(x-3)$
Write the product with every factor showing: $\frac{(x+6)(x+3)}{4(x-3)(x+3)}\times\frac{32x(x-3)}{2x(x+6)}$
Cancel the common factors $(x+6)$, $(x+3)$, $(x-3)$ and $x$: $=\frac{1}{4}\times\frac{32}{2}$
Multiply and simplify: $=\frac{32}{8}=4$

Put both numerators over the one common denominator and remove the brackets, multiplying every term inside each bracket. $\dfrac{5(x+5)}{10}+\dfrac{2(x+6)}{10}=\dfrac{5(x+5)+2(x+6)}{10}=\dfrac{5x+25+2x+12}{10}$
Collect the like terms in the numerator. $\dfrac{5x+25+2x+12}{10}=\dfrac{7x+37}{10}$
This cannot be simplified further, because the coefficient $7$ of $x$ and the denominator $10$ have no common factor. So $\dfrac{x+5}{2}+\dfrac{x+6}{5}=\dfrac{7x+37}{10}$.

questions.stem: If the following terms make a linear sequence: $\frac{-7k}{4}  + 1\;;\;\frac{-3k}{4}  + 2\;;\;\frac{-7k}{4}  + 6\;;\;\ldots$ determine the value of $k$ and hence the numeric value of the common difference of the sequence. Write your answer as a simplified fraction.

canonical_solution.text_md: In a linear sequence the common difference is the same all the way along, so $T_{2} - T_{1} = T_{3} - T_{2}$.
Put in the terms: $\left(\frac{-3k}{4}  + 2\right) - \left(\frac{-7k}{4}  + 1\right) = \left(\frac{-7k}{4}  + 6\right) - \left(\frac{-3k}{4}  + 2\right)$.
Multiply every term by $4$ to clear the fractions: $(-3k  + 8) - (-7k  + 4) = (-7k  + 24) - (-3k  + 8)$.
Simplify each side: $4k  + 4 = -4k  + 16$.
Collect the terms in $k$ on one side and the numbers on the other: $8k = 12$.
Divide both sides by $8$: $k = \frac{12}{8} = \frac{3}{2}$.

Now put $k = \frac{3}{2}$ into the terms: $T_{1} = -\frac{7}{4} \times \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)  + 1 = -\frac{13}{8}$, $T_{2} = -\frac{3}{4} \times \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)  + 2 = \frac{7}{8}$ and $T_{3} = -\frac{7}{4} \times \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)  + 6 = \frac{27}{8}$.

The common difference is $d = T_{2} - T_{1} = \left(\frac{7}{8}\right) - \left(-\frac{13}{8}\right) = \frac{5}{2}$. Check: $T_{3} - T_{2} = \left(\frac{27}{8}\right) - \left(\frac{7}{8}\right) = \frac{5}{2}$, which is the same.

Factorise the trinomial. Two numbers with product $-45$ and sum $4$ are $-5$ and $9$, so $(x-5)(x+9)=0$.
A product is zero only when one of its factors is zero, so $x=5$ or $x=-9$.

questions.stem: Solve for $a$ in $P = k\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}$ if $k = 2$, $b = 4$ and $P = 10$. Give both values of $a$.

canonical_solution.text_md: Divide both sides of $P = k\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}$ by $k$ so the square root stands alone: $\dfrac{P}{k} = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}$.
Square both sides to remove the square root: $\left(\dfrac{P}{k}\right)^2 = a^2 + b^2$.
Subtract $b^2$ from both sides: $a^2 = \left(\dfrac{P}{k}\right)^2 - b^2$.
Take the square root of both sides, writing both signs: $a = \pm\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{P}{k}\right)^2 - b^2}$.
Substitute $P = 10$, $k = 2$ and $b = 4$: $a = \pm\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{10}{2}\right)^2 - 4^2} = \pm\sqrt{5^2 - 4^2} = \pm\sqrt{9} = \pm3$.

canonical_solution.text_md: Test each statement by substituting $x = 14^\circ$ and $y = 76^\circ$ and working out its left-hand side (LHS) and its right-hand side (RHS) on a calculator in degree mode. A statement is true only if the two sides are equal.

$\sin^2 x + \cos^2(90^\circ - y) = 1$: LHS $= \sin^2 14^\circ + \cos^2(90^\circ - 76^\circ) = \sin^2 14^\circ + \cos^2 14^\circ \approx 0.0585 + 0.9415 \approx 1.00$ and RHS $= 1$. The two sides are equal, so this statement is true.
$\sin^2 x + \cos^2 y = 1$: LHS $= \sin^2 14^\circ + \cos^2 76^\circ \approx 0.0585 + 0.0585 \approx 0.12$ but RHS $= 1$. The two sides are not equal, so this statement is false.

$\cos(x + y) = \cos x + \cos y$: LHS $= \cos(14^\circ + 76^\circ) = \cos 90^\circ = 0$ but RHS $= \cos 14^\circ + \cos 76^\circ \approx 0.9703 + 0.2419 \approx 1.21$. The two sides are not equal, so this statement is false.
$\sin(90^\circ - x) = \sin x$: LHS $= \sin(90^\circ - 14^\circ) = \sin 76^\circ \approx 0.9703$ but RHS $= \sin 14^\circ \approx 0.2419$. The two sides are not equal, so this statement is false.
Only $\sin^2 x + \cos^2(90^\circ - y) = 1$ has two equal sides, so it is the true statement.

questions.stem: The angle $\theta$ is acute and $\tan\theta=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\mathrm{1}}$. Without a calculator, which of the following is the value of $\cos\theta$?

canonical_solution.text_md: List the values of $\tan$ at the special angles, from the triangle with sides $1$, $1$, $\sqrt{2}$ and the triangle with sides $1$, $2$, $\sqrt{3}$: $\tan30^{\circ}=\frac{\mathrm{1}}{\sqrt{3}}$, $\tan45^{\circ}=\frac{\mathrm{1}}{\mathrm{1}}$ and $\tan60^{\circ}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\mathrm{1}}$.
The given value $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\mathrm{1}}$ matches only $\tan60^{\circ}$, so $\theta=60^{\circ}$.
Now find the ratio that was asked for at this angle: $\cos\theta=\cos60^{\circ}=\frac{\mathrm{1}}{\mathrm{2}}$.
So $\cos\theta=\frac{\mathrm{1}}{\mathrm{2}}$. The value $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\mathrm{1}}$ belongs to $\tan\theta$, so it is not the value of $\cos\theta$.

questions.stem: In the right-angled triangle $ABC$ the right angle is at $B$, $AB = \frac{15}{\sqrt{7}}$, $BC = 5$ and $AC = \frac{20}{\sqrt{7}}$. Let $\theta$ be the angle at $A$. Solve for $\tan{\theta}$ in surd form.

$\tan{\theta}=\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}=\frac{5}{\frac{15}{\sqrt{7}}}$
Dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal: $\tan{\theta}=5\times\frac{\sqrt{7}}{15}=\frac{5\sqrt{7}}{15}$
Cancel the common factor $5$: $\tan{\theta}=\frac{\sqrt{7}}{3}$

questions.stem: $P$ is a point with co-ordinates $(-8, 9)$ on a Cartesian plane, and $O$ is the origin. $OP$ forms an angle, $\theta$, measured anticlockwise from the positive $x$-axis. Determine $\text{cosec}\theta$ without using a calculator.

canonical_solution.text_md: Read off the co-ordinates of $P$ and keep their signs: $x=-8$ and $y=9$. The point lies in quadrant 2.
We find $r=OP$ with the theorem of Pythagoras. $r$ is a length, so it is positive in every quadrant: $\begin{aligned}r^{2}&=x^{2}+y^{2}\\&=(-8)^{2}+(9)^{2}\\&=145\\r&=\sqrt{145}\end{aligned}$
The reciprocal ratio $\text{cosec}\theta$ is $r$ over $y$: $\begin{aligned}\text{cosec}\theta&=\frac{r}{y}\\&=\frac{\sqrt{145}}{9}\end{aligned}$

canonical_solution.text_md: Read off the co-ordinates of $P$ and keep their signs: $x=9$ and $y=1$.
We find $r=OP$ with the theorem of Pythagoras. $r$ is a length, so it is positive: $\begin{aligned}r^{2}&=x^{2}+y^{2}\\&=(9)^{2}+(1)^{2}\\&=82\\r&=\sqrt{82}\end{aligned}$
Write each ratio with $x$, $y$ and $r$: $\begin{aligned}\sin\theta&=\frac{y}{r}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{82}}\\\cos\theta&=\frac{x}{r}=\frac{9}{\sqrt{82}}\end{aligned}$
Multiply the two ratios. $\sqrt{82}\times\sqrt{82}=82$, so the surds disappear: $\begin{aligned}\sin\theta\cos\theta&=\frac{1}{\sqrt{82}}\times\frac{9}{\sqrt{82}}\\&=\frac{9}{82}\end{aligned}$
The numerator and the denominator have no common factor, so the fraction is in simplest form: $\sin\theta\cos\theta=\frac{9}{82}$

Find the $x$-intercept by letting $y=0$: $-6x = 30$, so $x = -5$. The $x$-intercept is $-5$.

To decide whether the graph is increasing or decreasing, write the equation in the form $y=mx+c$. Move the $x$-term to the other side of the equals sign (it changes sign) and divide every term by $5$. This gives $m = \frac{6}{5}$ and $c = 6$, which agrees with the $y$-intercept found above.
The gradient $m = \frac{6}{5}$ is positive, so the graph is increasing. The sign in front of $x$ in the given equation is not the sign of $m$, because the $x$-term had to change sides.
The line passes through $(-5, 0)$ and $(0, 6)$, so plot those two points and join them. Answer: $x$-intercept $= -5$, $y$-intercept $= 6$; the graph is increasing.

questions.stem: Given the following equation: $y=-\frac{5}{x}+6$ Determine: (a) the $x$-coordinate of the $x$-intercept (as a fraction in lowest terms if it is not a whole number); (b) the one value that $x$ can never take, that is, the value excluded from the domain; (c) the one value that $y$ can never take, that is, the value excluded from the range. Give your three answers in the order (a), (b), (c), separated by commas.

canonical_solution.text_md: To find the $x$-intercept, let $y=0$: $0=-\frac{5}{x}+6$.
Multiply both sides by $x$ (the equation is undefined for $x=0$, so $x\neq 0$): $0=-5+6x$.
Move the constant term to the other side: $6x=5$.
Divide both sides by $6$: $x=\frac{5}{6}=\frac{5}{6}$, so the $x$-intercept is $\left(\frac{5}{6}, 0\right)$.
Domain: the denominator cannot be $0$, so $x$ can be any real number except $0$: $\{x: x\in\mathbb{R},\ x\neq 0\}$.
Range: the fraction $-\frac{5}{x}$ can never equal $0$, so $y$ can never equal $6$: $\{y: y\in\mathbb{R},\ y\neq 6\}$.
So the $x$-coordinate of the $x$-intercept is $\frac{5}{6}$, $x$ can never be $0$, and $y$ can never be $6$.

canonical_solution.text_md: At the $x$-intercept the graph meets the $x$-axis, so $y = 0$. Substitute: $0 = \frac{-6}{x} - 1$.
Move the constant term to the other side: $\frac{-6}{x} = 1$.
Multiply both sides by $x$ (we know $x \neq 0$ because $x = 0$ is the vertical asymptote): $-6 = (1) \cdot x$.
Divide both sides by $1$: $x = -6$.
The $x$-intercept is $(-6, 0)$. There is no $y$-intercept, because $x = 0$ is an asymptote.

canonical_solution.text_md: The horizontal asymptote of $y=\frac{a}{x}+q$ is the line $y=q$. Here the asymptote is $y=2$, so $q=2$.
Substitute $q=2$ and the coordinates of A, $x=-2$ and $y=\frac{5}{2}$, into $y=\frac{a}{x}+q$: $\frac{5}{2}=\frac{a}{-2} + 2$.
Multiply both sides by $-2$ to clear the fraction: $\left(-2\right)\times\left(\frac{5}{2}\right)=\left[\frac{a}{-2} + 2\right]\times\left(-2\right)$, so $-5=a - 4$.
Solve for $a$: $a=-5 + 4=-1$.
Therefore $a=-1$ and $q=2$.

Move the constant to the right-hand side: $-9\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^x = -3$.
Divide both sides by $-9$: $\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^x = \frac{1}{3}$.
Write $\frac{1}{3}$ as a power of $\frac{1}{3}$: $\frac{1}{3} = \left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{1}$.
The bases are equal, so the exponents are equal: $x = 1$. The graph cuts the $x$-axis at $(1, 0)$.

canonical_solution.text_md: Use $\cos 0^\circ = 1$ and $\cos 180^\circ = -1$: $f(0^\circ) = a + q$ and $f(180^\circ) = -a + q$.
The two given points say $a + q = 8$ and $-a + q = -2$.
Subtract the second equation from the first: $2a = f(0^\circ) - f(180^\circ) = 10$.
Divide by 2: $a = 5$.

Check: the highest and lowest values of the graph are $10$ units apart, so the amplitude is half of that, $5$, and this equals $|a|$. A positive $a$ makes the graph start at its highest point and a negative $a$ makes it start at its lowest point.

To find $a$, substitute $q=-4$ and point $B$, $\left(45^{\circ}, -2\right)$, into the equation. Remember that $\tan 45^{\circ}=1$.
$\begin{aligned}y&=a\tan\theta-4\\-2&=a\tan45^{\circ}-4\\-2&=a(1)-4\\-2+4&=a\\2&=a\end{aligned}$
Therefore $a=2$ and $q=-4$.

canonical_solution.text_md: The sine and the cosine of any angle lie between $-1$ and $1$: $-1 \le \operatorname{sin}\theta \le 1$.

Now add the constant $-3$ to every part. The lowest value of $y$ is $-3 - 3 = -6$ and the highest value of $y$ is $-3 + 3 = 0$.
So the range is $-6 \le y \le 0$. The negative sign of $a$ changes which value of $\operatorname{sin}\theta$ gives the lowest $y$, but the range is still $3$ below and $3$ above $-3$.

The points $A$ and $C$ lie on the left-hand side of the transversal, and $B$ and $D$ on its right-hand side. It is given that $A\hat{P}S = (2x + 21)^\circ$ and $D\hat{Q}T = (4x - 13)^\circ$. Calculate the size of $A\hat{P}Q$, in degrees.

canonical_solution.text_md: $A\hat{P}S = B\hat{P}Q$ (vertically opposite angles).
$B\hat{P}Q = C\hat{Q}P$ (alternate angles; $AB \parallel CD$).
$C\hat{Q}P = D\hat{Q}T$ (vertically opposite angles). Therefore $A\hat{P}S = D\hat{Q}T$.
So $2x + 21 = 4x - 13$, which gives $2x = 34$ and $x = \frac{34}{2} = 17$.
$A\hat{P}S = (2 \times 17 + 21)^\circ = 55^\circ$.
$A\hat{P}Q + A\hat{P}S = 180^\circ$ (angles on a straight line $SQ$), so $A\hat{P}Q = 180^\circ - 55^\circ = 125^\circ$.

In $\triangle FGH$ and $\triangle JKH$: $FH = JH$ (given), $GH = KH$ (given) and $\angle FHG = \angle JHK$ (vertically opposite). So $\triangle FGH \equiv \triangle JKH$ (SAS).
The letters are in matching order, so $F$ matches $J$ and $G$ matches $K$. Therefore $\angle JKH = \angle FGH$.

canonical_solution.text_md: Work out for how many years the money was invested: $n=15-6=9$ years.
Write down the given information: $\begin{aligned}A&=\text{R4900}\\P&=\text{R4000}\\n&=9\\i&=?\end{aligned}$
The interest is simple, so use $A=P(1+in)$ and make $i$ the subject: $\begin{aligned}A&=P(1+in)\\\frac{A}{P}&=1+in\\\frac{A}{P}-1&=in\\\frac{\frac{A}{P}-1}{n}&=i\end{aligned}$
Substitute the values: $i=\frac{\frac{4900}{4000}-1}{9}=\frac{900}{36000}=0.025$
Write $i$ as a percentage: $i=0.025\times100=2.5\%$ per year.
So the money was invested at a simple interest rate of $2.5\%$ per annum.

At the end of $6$ years Thandi's investment is worth $\text{R 13219.12}$ more than Sipho's.

Write down the given information for Sipho's investment: $\begin{aligned}P_2&=4760\\i_2&=\frac{6.9}{100}=0.069\\n&=4\\A_2&=?\end{aligned}$

Thandi's accumulated amount is found with $A=P(1+i)^n$. Do not round part-way: use the full calculator value and round only the amount itself to two decimal places. $\begin{aligned}A_1&=P_1(1+i_1)^n\\&=6760\left(1+0.054\right)^{4}\\&=\text{R 8342.75}\end{aligned}$
Sipho's accumulated amount is found the same way: $\begin{aligned}A_2&=P_2(1+i_2)^n\\&=4760\left(1+0.069\right)^{4}\\&=\text{R 6216.10}\end{aligned}$
To see how much more Thandi's investment is worth, subtract Sipho's accumulated amount from Thandi's: $\begin{aligned}A_1-A_2&=8342.75-6216.10\\&=\text{R 2126.65}\end{aligned}$

questions.stem: Morgan invests $\text{R5000}$ into an account which pays out a lump sum at the end of $4$ years. If he gets $\text{R10368.00}$ at the end of the period, what compound interest rate did the bank offer him? The interest is compounded annually. Give the rate as a percentage per annum, as a number without the % sign.

canonical_solution.text_md: Write down what is given: $A=\text{R10368.00}$, $P=\text{R5000}$, $n=4$ and $i=\,?$
Write down the formula and substitute the known values: $A=P(1+i)^{n}$ gives $\text{R10368.00}=\text{R5000}(1+i)^{4}$
Divide both sides by $\text{R5000}$ to get the bracket on its own: $\frac{10368.00}{5000}=(1+i)^{4}$
Take the $n$th root of both sides (here $n=4$) and use your calculator: $1+i=\sqrt[4]{\frac{10368.00}{5000}}=1.20$
Subtract $1$ from both sides to find $i$: $i=1.20-1=0.20$
Write the rate as a percentage: $i\times 100=20$, so the bank offered a compound interest rate of $20$ % p.a.
Check: $\text{R5000}\times(1.20)^{4}=\text{R10368.00}$, which is the amount Morgan received.
